title: From Seoul to Wall Street: A Chip Sell-Off Pushes the Nasdaq Into a Correction
body:
The sell-off that began in Seoul on Thursday did not stay there. The KOSPI fell 5.3% to 5,383.80 as foreign investors sold a net 3.4 trillion won of shares, and hours later the slide **sent shockwaves through** Wall Street. The Nasdaq Composite tumbled 5.5% to 24,315, its worst day since April 2025, which pushed the index into a **correction**, or a drop of more than 10% from its recent peak. The S&P 500 lost 4.4%, while chipmakers **bore the brunt of** the damage: Nvidia and Qualcomm each dropped more than 9%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged about 12%.

Most analysts **attributed** the rout (폭락) **to** politics rather than profits. Only a day after Wall Street had cheered the Democratic sweep in the midterm elections, the same result was suddenly seen as a sign that AI companies could face tighter regulation. Given the **magnitude** of the drop, some funds must have been forced to sell their winners simply to raise cash. Money rushed into safer assets in a classic **flight to quality**, lifting gold to about $4,098 an ounce and pulling the 10-year Treasury yield down to 4.84%. Meanwhile, the VIX, Wall Street's fear gauge, jumped nearly 70% to 28.2.

Although the KOSPI has already lost almost 21% in 20 trading days, Korean stocks might not be spared again today. If the **contagion** (전염·확산) spreads, even sectors that have little to do with AI could be dragged lower.
ko:
목요일 서울에서 시작된 매도는 거기서 멈추지 않았다. 외국인이 3.4조 원을 순매도하면서 코스피는 5.3% 내린 5,383.80에 마감했고, 몇 시간 뒤 그 하락은 월가에 충격파를 보냈다. 나스닥 종합지수는 5.5% 급락한 24,315로 2025년 4월 이후 최악의 하루를 기록했고, 이로써 최근 고점 대비 10% 넘게 빠진 '조정' 국면에 들어섰다. S&P 500은 4.4% 내렸고, 피해를 가장 크게 떠안은 것은 반도체였다. 엔비디아와 퀄컴이 각각 9% 넘게 떨어졌고 필라델피아 반도체지수는 약 12% 폭락했다.

대부분의 애널리스트는 이번 폭락의 원인을 실적이 아니라 정치로 봤다. 월가가 중간선거 민주당 압승에 환호한 지 불과 하루 만에, 같은 결과가 갑자기 AI 기업들이 더 강한 규제를 받을 수 있다는 신호로 받아들여졌다. 하락 폭을 고려하면, 일부 펀드는 단지 현금을 마련하려고 수익 난 종목까지 팔 수밖에 없었을 것이다. 돈은 전형적인 '안전자산 선호(질적 도피)' 흐름 속에 더 안전한 자산으로 몰려, 금값은 온스당 약 4,098달러로 올랐고 미 10년물 국채 금리는 4.84%로 내려갔다. 한편 월가의 공포지수 VIX는 70% 가까이 뛰어 28.2가 됐다.

코스피가 이미 20거래일 동안 약 21% 빠졌지만, 오늘 한국 주식이 또다시 피해를 비켜 가지 못할 수도 있다. 이 전염이 퍼진다면 AI와 거의 관계없는 업종까지 끌려 내려갈 수 있다.

vocab.ko: (증시) 조정 — 최근 고점 대비 10% 이상 하락
vocab.en_easy: A fall of more than 10% from a recent high, which is smaller than a crash but bigger than a normal dip.
vocab.ex: The Nasdaq entered a correction on Thursday, so I'm not adding to my tech positions until things calm down.

vocab.en_easy: When trouble in one market or country quickly spreads to others, like a disease.
vocab.ex: Korean investors worried about contagion from Wall Street's chip sell-off.

vocab.ko: 안전자산 선호(위험자산 → 국채·금 등으로 자금 이동)
vocab.en_easy: When scared investors move money out of risky assets and into safe ones such as government bonds or gold.
vocab.ex: The flight to quality pushed bond prices up and yields down.

vocab.en_easy: How big or serious something is.
vocab.ex: I didn't realize the magnitude of the problem until my whole team had to work over the weekend.

vocab.ko: A를 B 탓(덕)으로 돌리다, A의 원인을 B로 보다
vocab.en_easy: To say that something was caused by a particular thing.
vocab.ex: I attribute my better sleep to walking for 30 minutes after dinner.

vocab.en_easy: To suffer the worst part of something bad.
vocab.ex: Chip stocks bore the brunt of the sell-off, while utilities barely moved.

vocab.en_easy: To shock and upset a whole group or place very suddenly.
vocab.ex: The news that our favorite café was closing sent shockwaves through the whole neighborhood.

grammar.point: 수동태 (be + p.p. · 조동사 + be p.p. · be seen as / be forced to)
grammar.quote: the same result was suddenly seen as a sign that AI companies could face tighter regulation … Korean stocks might not be spared again today.
grammar.explain_ko: 주어가 행동을 '당하는' 쪽이면 be + p.p. 결과(result)는 사람에 의해 '여겨지는' 대상 → was seen as. 조동사가 붙으면 조동사 + be + p.p.(might not be spared = 피해를 면하지 못할 수도). 'be seen as ~(~로 여겨지다)', 'be forced to ~(~할 수밖에 없다)'는 수동태 덩어리로 외워 두면 말하기에 바로 쓴다.
examples: The rally was seen as a relief bounce rather than a real recovery.
(OPIc) The park near my place was renovated last year, so now it's really nice to walk around.

grammar.point: 조동사 추측 (must have p.p. · might · could)
grammar.quote: some funds must have been forced to sell their winners simply to raise cash … even sectors that have little to do with AI could be dragged lower.
grammar.explain_ko: must have p.p. = '(과거에) ~했음이 틀림없다' 강한 추측 — 하락 폭(magnitude)을 근거로 과거를 추론. might / could + 동사원형 = 현재·미래의 약한 가능성(~할 수도 있다). 확신 정도: must have p.p.(거의 확실) > might/could(반반 이하). 반대로 should have p.p.는 '~했어야 했는데(후회)'라 의미가 다르다.
examples: Given how fast the index fell, a lot of people must have panicked at the open.
(OPIc) I must have walked about ten kilometers that day, because my legs were sore for two days.

tense.sentence: Only a day after Wall Street had cheered the Democratic sweep in the midterm elections, the same result was suddenly seen as a sign …
tense.why_ko: '환호한 것(수요일)'이 '다르게 해석된 것(목요일)'보다 먼저 → 더 이전 과거는 had p.p.; 주절은 과거 시점의 수동.

tense.sentence: Although the KOSPI has already lost almost 21% in 20 trading days, …
tense.why_ko: 20거래일 전부터 '지금까지' 누적된 하락 → 현재와 연결된 기간 = has p.p. (특정 과거 시점 yesterday 가 있으면 과거형).

review.q: After such a wild week, I'd rather ________ before I buy anything new. 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 자연스러운 표현은?
review.exp_ko: '사기 전에 ~하고 싶다' + 정신없던 한 주 → 상황이 가라앉길 기다리다 = let the dust settle(②). ① 오르는 걸 쫓아 사는 건 '기다린다'와 반대 ③ turn on a dime 은 '급방향 전환'이라 주어가 시장일 때 쓴다 ④ 일찍 자러 가다 — 매수 맥락과 무관.

review.q: Despite the noisy headlines, the underlying demand for memory chips remains strong. 밑줄 친 underlying 과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것은?
review.exp_ko: underlying = 겉의 소음 아래 깔린 '근본적인' → fundamental(④). ① 단기 ② 발표된 ③ 계절적 — 모두 수요를 꾸밀 수 있어 그럴듯하지만, 'Despite the noisy headlines(겉 소음과 대조)' 구조에는 '밑바탕의'가 맞다.

review.q: Selling everything after one scary headline is a ________ reaction that you'll probably regret later. 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
review.exp_ko: 헤드라인 하나에 '반사적으로' 전부 판다 + 나중에 후회 → knee-jerk(①). ② 늦은 반응이면 '헤드라인 하나 뒤 즉시'와 안 맞음 ③ measured(신중한)는 후회와 모순 ④ mixed(엇갈린)는 '전부 판다'와 모순.

quiz.q:
[어휘] 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
"The Nasdaq Composite tumbled 5.5% to 24,315, which pushed the index into a ________, or a drop of more than 10% from its recent peak."
quiz.exp_ko: 빈칸 뒤 'or(즉) 최근 고점 대비 10% 넘는 하락'이 정의 → 증시 용어 correction(③). ① reversal 은 추세 '방향 전환' 일반 ② downturn 은 경기·매출의 막연한 하강(10% 기준 없음) ④ recession 은 '경기침체'로 지수가 아니라 경제 전체에 쓴다.

quiz.q:
[어법] 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
"①Hitting hardest by the election news, chipmakers led the decline. Analysts said the regulatory risk ②had not been priced in, and some funds ③must have been forced to sell. If the contagion spreads, Korean stocks ④might not be spared."
choices: ② had not been priced in
quiz.exp_ko: 반도체주는 뉴스에 '타격을 받은' 쪽(수동) + 뒤에 by → 과거분사 Hit hardest 가 맞다(①). ② 말한 시점보다 먼저 + 위험이 '반영되지 않은' 수동 → had not been p.p. ✓ ③ 과거 추측 + 수동 = must have been p.p. ✓ ④ 조동사 + be + p.p. 수동 ✓.

quiz.q: [요지] 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: A disappointing earnings season for chipmakers dragged Wall Street into a correction.
Fears over AI regulation hit chip stocks, yet safe assets and Korean stocks held steady.
The steep fall in chip stocks reflected losses that funds had built up over many months.
Election-driven regulatory fears spread a chip sell-off across markets, and the risk to Korea remains.
quiz.exp_ko: 주제문(서울→월가로 번진 매도) + 원인(실적 아닌 정치·규제) + 결론(한국도 또 맞을 수 있다) → ④. ① 본문은 'politics rather than profits' — 실적이 원인이라는 건 정반대 ② 코스피도 −5.3%로 '버텼다'가 틀림(금은 오름) ③ 펀드 강제 매도는 must have 로 한 줄 추측일 뿐 글 전체 요지가 아님.

choices: The KOSPI fell by a larger percentage on Thursday than the Nasdaq did.
The chip index fell more than twice as much as the Nasdaq in percentage terms.
Before its jump, the VIX stood above 20.
The S&P 500 fell more than the KOSPI did on the day.

talk.topic: Worst day since April 2025 — 나스닥 조정 진입, 금요일 아침 코스피는?
talk.setting_ko: 금요일 아침 출근길, 투자하는 동료 둘이 밤사이 미국장 결과를 보며 이야기한다.

dialogue.en: Did you see what happened overnight? The Nasdaq got hammered — down five and a half percent.
dialogue.ko: 밤사이 봤어? 나스닥 완전 두들겨 맞았어. 5.5% 빠졌대.

dialogue.en: Yeah, and chips were the worst. Nvidia was down more than nine percent. It was a perfect storm.
dialogue.ko: 응, 반도체가 제일 심했어. 엔비디아가 9% 넘게 빠졌더라. 악재가 다 겹쳤지.

dialogue.en: What gets me is that we already dropped five percent here yesterday. Now we're probably getting hit again.
dialogue.ko: 내가 답답한 건 우리 어제 이미 5% 빠졌잖아. 오늘 또 맞을 것 같아.

dialogue.en: Honestly, where it bottoms out is anyone's guess. I'm staying on the sidelines today.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히 바닥이 어디일지는 아무도 몰라. 난 오늘 그냥 관망할래.

dialogue.en: Same here. I set my buying levels last week, so I'm just going to stick to the plan.
dialogue.ko: 나도. 지난주에 매수 가격대 정해 뒀으니까 그냥 계획대로 할 거야.

dialogue.en: Smart. Making it up as you go on a day like this never ends well.
dialogue.ko: 현명하네. 이런 날 즉흥으로 하면 끝이 안 좋더라.

dialogue.en: Let's check back at lunch and see how bad the opening was.
dialogue.ko: 점심때 다시 보고 시초가가 얼마나 나빴는지 보자.

expressions.ex: Tech stocks got hammered after the election results.

expressions.when_ko: 나쁜 요인 여러 개가 동시에 터졌을 때
expressions.ex: Bad weather, a flat tire, and a missed train — it was a perfect storm.

expressions.when_ko: 결과를 전혀 예상할 수 없을 때
expressions.ex: Where the market goes next is anyone's guess.
I'm staying on the sidelines until the volatility calms down.

expressions.when_ko: 감정에 흔들리지 않고 정해 둔 대로 할 때
expressions.ex: Even when it rains, I stick to the plan and walk on the treadmill instead.

your_turn.q_en: When the market drops sharply, what do you usually do? Do you buy, sell, or just wait?
your_turn.hint_ko: 현재 시제 습관 + 이유 1개 + 과거 사례 1개(must have p.p. 로 추측 한 줄). 'stay on the sidelines', 'stick to the plan' 넣기.
your_turn.sample_answer: Well, these days I mostly stick to the plan. I set my buying levels in advance, so when the market drops, I don't have to decide anything in a panic. A few years ago, I sold everything on a really bad day, and the market bounced back the very next week. I must have lost a lot just because I was scared. So now, if I'm not sure, I just stay on the sidelines and wait.

talk.topic: 퇴근 후 동네 한 바퀴 — 친구와 만보 걷기 챌린지 (Background Survey #47 걷기)
talk.setting_ko: 퇴근 후, 같은 동네 사는 친구가 걷기 앱 챌린지를 같이 하자고 제안한다.

dialogue.en: Hey, I've been sitting all day. I really need to stretch my legs. Want to go for a walk?
dialogue.ko: 야, 하루 종일 앉아 있었어. 다리 좀 풀어야겠다. 산책 갈래?

dialogue.en: Sure, I could use some fresh air too. I'm only at four thousand steps today.
dialogue.ko: 좋아, 나도 바람 좀 쐬고 싶었어. 오늘 아직 4천 보밖에 안 걸었어.

dialogue.en: Then let's do the stream trail. One loop is about five thousand steps, so you'll get your steps in.
dialogue.ko: 그럼 하천 산책로 가자. 한 바퀴가 5천 보쯤이니까 오늘 걸음 수 채울 거야.

dialogue.en: Perfect. Oh, have you tried that walking challenge in the app? Ten thousand steps a day for a month.
dialogue.ko: 딱이다. 아, 앱에 걷기 챌린지 해 봤어? 한 달 동안 하루 만 보.

dialogue.en: Not yet, but count me in. It'd be a nice change from the gym.
dialogue.ko: 아직. 근데 나도 끼워 줘. 헬스장 말고 좋은 변화가 될 것 같아.

dialogue.en: Great. Just don't blame me when we lose track of time and get home at ten.
dialogue.ko: 좋아. 대신 시간 가는 줄 모르고 걷다가 10시에 들어가도 내 탓 하지 마.

dialogue.en: Ha, honestly, after today, that sounds like a breath of fresh air.
dialogue.ko: 하하, 오늘 같은 날엔 그게 오히려 숨통 트이는 일이지.

expressions.ko: (오래 앉아 있다가) 다리 좀 풀다, 잠깐 걷다
expressions.when_ko: 오래 앉아 있었거나 이동 중에 잠깐 걷고 싶을 때
expressions.ex: On long drives, I stop every hour to stretch my legs.
I take the stairs at work to get my steps in.
I could use a coffee right now.

expressions.when_ko: 뭔가에 빠져 시간이 훌쩍 지났을 때
expressions.ex: We were talking so much that we lost track of time.

expressions.when_ko: 지루하거나 답답한 것과 대비되는 반가운 변화를 말할 때
expressions.ex: Walking to work instead of taking the subway was a breath of fresh air.

your_turn.q_en: Where do you usually go for a walk, and how often do you go? Describe a typical walk.
your_turn.hint_ko: 장소(동네 하천·공원) 묘사 → 빈도·시간 → 걸으며 하는 것(음악·통화) → 느낌. 'stretch my legs', 'get my steps in' 넣기.
your_turn.sample_answer: Well, I usually go for a walk along the stream near my apartment, maybe three or four times a week after work. It's a flat, quiet trail with trees on both sides, so it's perfect for stretching my legs after sitting all day. One loop takes about forty minutes, which is enough to get my steps in. I usually listen to music or a podcast, and sometimes I call my mom. By the time I get home, I feel much lighter and calmer.

opic.survey_topic: 금요일 — 셀프 소개 + 주간 복습 콤보 (걷기 #47 · 이번 주 조깅 #46·음악 #23 표현 재활용)

combo.q_en: Let's start the interview now. Tell me a little bit about yourself.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(한 줄 소개) → 본문 ① 일·생활 리듬 ② 취미 2개(걷기·헬스 — 서베이 주제와 연결해 다음 질문 복선) ③ 성격 한 줄 + 예시 → 마무리(요즘 목표). 60~90초. 채점 포인트: 문장 나열이 아닌 '문단' 흐름, 현재 시제 일관, 구체 디테일(시간·장소·숫자).
combo.model_answer: Okay, let me introduce myself. I'm a guy in my early thirties, and I work at an office in Seoul, so, you know, my weekdays are pretty routine. I sit in front of a computer most of the day, which is exactly why I try to stay active after work. I'm really into two things these days. The first one is working out. I go to the gym near my place, and I'm pretty serious about it — I even track my sets and weights in an app. The second one is walking. There's a stream trail right next to my apartment, and I walk there a few nights a week, usually with music on. Oh, and I've also started investing a little, so I check the market news every morning on my way to work. As for my personality, I'd say I'm a planner. I mean, I like to set a goal and stick to the plan. Right now, my goal is to get my English back to where it used to be. So, yeah, that's me in a nutshell.

key_phrases.en: I'm really into two things these days.
key_phrases.ko: 요즘 두 가지에 푹 빠져 있어요.

key_phrases.en: As for my personality, I'd say ~

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '저는 ~입니다' 나열, IH는 'which is exactly why'처럼 이유로 문장을 잇고, AL은 자기소개 안에 다음 질문(헬스·걷기) 복선을 깔아 담화를 설계한다.

combo.q_en: In your background survey, you indicated that you enjoy taking walks. Where do you usually go for a walk? Who do you go with, and what do you usually do during your walk? Tell me about your walking routine in as much detail as possible.
combo.q_ko: 서베이에서 걷기를 좋아한다고 하셨는데요. 주로 어디로 걷나요? 누구와 가고, 걸으면서 주로 뭘 하나요? 걷기 루틴을 최대한 자세히 말해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(언제·어디) → 본문 ① 준비(옷·이어폰·앱) ② 코스 묘사(시각·소리) ③ 걸으며 하는 것 + 이유 → 마무리(끝나고 하는 것·기분). 현재 시제 + usually/sometimes 빈도부사. 헬스 연결: 'active recovery', 'my calves and hamstrings loosen up' 같은 근육 디테일로 구체성 점수.
combo.model_answer: Well, I usually go for a walk right after dinner, maybe three or four times a week. Before I head out, I change into comfortable sneakers, grab my earphones, and open my walking app, because I'm trying to get my steps in every day. My go-to spot is the stream trail near my apartment. It's a flat path with trees on both sides, and at night it's lit up by these little lamps, so it feels really peaceful. Most of the time I go alone and listen to music — actually, I've been hooked on a new playlist lately. But on Fridays, my friend sometimes joins me, and we just chat about work or the stock market. Oh, and since I lift weights on most days, I treat walking as active recovery. You know, after a heavy leg day, a slow walk really helps my calves and hamstrings loosen up. When I get home, I take a quick shower, and honestly, I sleep so much better on the days I walk.

key_phrases.en: I treat walking as active recovery.

key_phrases.ko: 하체 운동을 세게 한 날 다음에

key_phrases.en: I sleep so much better on the days I ~

combo.level_up_ko: IH는 루틴을 순서대로 말하고, AL은 '왜 그렇게 하는지(active recovery, 수면)'를 루틴 중간중간 끼워 넣어 이유-결과가 있는 문단으로 만든다.

combo.q_en: Tell me about a memorable walk you have taken. When was it, and where did you go? Who were you with, and what made that walk so memorable?
combo.q_ko: 기억에 남는 산책 경험을 말해 주세요. 언제 어디로 갔고, 누구와 함께였으며, 왜 그렇게 기억에 남나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(언제·어디·누구) → 본문 ① 배경(왜 걷게 됐나) ② 사건(예상 밖 일 — 과거완료로 '그 전에 이미') ③ 감정 변화 → 마무리(지금 돌아보면). 과거 시제 일관 + 과거완료 1회 + must have p.p. 추측 1회로 AL 시제 범위 보여 주기.
combo.model_answer: Oh, I remember one walk really clearly. It was last spring, on a Sunday, and I was with my younger brother. We had planned to take a bus to a café across the river, but, um, the bus never came — there must have been some kind of accident on the road. So we just said, 'Okay, let's walk.' We ended up walking along the Han River for, like, two hours. At first, I was kind of annoyed, because I had already been to the gym that morning and my legs were tired. But then the cherry blossoms were everywhere, and the sun was going down, and we started talking about stuff we hadn't talked about in years — our childhood, our parents, his job. I mean, we're both busy, so we rarely get that kind of time. By the time we got to the café, it was almost closed. But honestly, it didn't matter. Looking back, that bus not showing up was the best thing that happened that day.

key_phrases.en: We ended up ~ing for, like, two hours.
~ was the best thing that happened that day.

combo.level_up_ko: IH는 과거 시제를 끝까지 지키고, AL은 had planned·must have been 처럼 '시제 층'을 섞고 마지막에 현재 시점의 해석(Looking back)으로 닫는다.

useful.en: Let me think about how to put this.
useful.ko: 이걸 어떻게 말할지 좀 생각해 볼게요.
useful.when_ko: 답이 바로 안 나올 때 자연스럽게 시간 벌기

useful.en: What I like most about it is ~
I'd never thought about it that way until ~
useful.ko: ~ 전까지는 그렇게 생각해 본 적이 없어요
useful.when_ko: 과거 경험 마무리에 깨달음을 붙일 때(과거완료)

opic.practice_ko: 금요일 주간 복습: 자기소개(1번)를 녹음 → 바로 이어 2번 걷기 루틴을 같은 녹음에서 2분 안에. 듣고 '이유 문장(because/which is why)'이 몇 번 나왔는지 세어 3번 미만이면 다시. 이번 주 표현(veg out·get my steps in·stick to the plan) 중 2개를 일부러 넣어 본다.
